why: D1 in code smoke: lens push at a forced cell
cases: code_positions: the first n scenes (scene order) answered right in every competence prompt of both families by none; both families on each scene
sets:
Stages run statement_positions' map, parts and readwrite unchanged (its transit rule, J-space split, lens push and
decision rule), on these cases (its module constants set for the two families; this script's own competence, figures,
report and examples). Map layers 28-44 every 2 on the 27B; parts and readwrite at the map's transit cells on its coarse
grid below the answer onset (28, 32, 36, 40), primary 32-40.
read: J-lens readout of the clean run at the set's positions: the bridge's best rank among word tokens (any single-token surface; formatting tokens removed) over the positions; X's the same (the floor)

families_meaning.KL: stated in code → prompt: a variable holds the country, its number looked up in the program's dict
families_meaning.KR: stated in code → memory: a variable holds the country, its capital recalled

d1code_decision:
Stages:  make (tokenizer; data/code_positions_v1/items.json)  verify  check
         manifest_competence --name N --why W [--limit K]  competence --name N   (GPU)
         plan [--n K]   map --name M --why W [--n K] [--layers ...]   parts --name P --map M --why W [--force SET:LAYER ...]
         readwrite --name R --map M --parts P --why W [--force ...]   figures --name R   examples --name M [--k 3]
Eligibility: BJ_D1CODE_COMPETENCE names the competence run (default d1code_competence_27b; "none": every scene, a smoke).
question: At the transit cells, does the J-lens read the bridge, and can its direction write it?
write: v_X - v_I (unit lens vectors), per position scaled to the norm of C's copy there times each scale; control: a random direction per position at the same norm; C's copy itself
decision:
Decision rule (fixed before the 27B run; per family, set and window, primary layers decide):
  J-space verdict (frac): inside if the concentration's lower bound > INSIDE (1.2) and above the random-dictionary
  null's upper bound; around if its upper bound < OUTSIDE (1.0) and not_jspace - jspace > 0 (paired bootstrap lower
  bound); else inconclusive. suite_split's own rule (inside above 2.0) is reported as verdict_strict.
  Lens write: written if at some scale <= 4x the lens direction flips >= 30% and beats the random direction (paired
  bootstrap lower bound of the flip difference > 0); not written if at every scale (0.5-16x) the difference's upper
  bound is < 0.10; else inconclusive.
  H-loc (location artefact) is supported for a lookup-used bound family (BL, BLR) if at a statement set in transit at
  the primary layers its J-space verdict is inside and the lens writes it there. H-around is supported if at every
  statement set in transit at the primary layers its J-space verdict is around and the lens does not write it, while
  the positive control at the same set and layers (countries B, else BR) is inside; without a passing positive control
  an 'around' result at the statements is not interpretable. No statement set of BL in transit at the primary layers:
  H-loc's location premise fails at the question-token layers (the secondary layers are reported, not decisive).
  Paired readers: at statement sets BL and BR (and BLR and BRL) get the identical patch on the same scenes (the context
  precedes the question), so their concentration difference isolates what the reader uses; reported with a scene
  bootstrap.
